oracle: The palm-leaf oracle of Hermes and Isis (P.Oxy. 886 = PGM XXIVa), Oxyrhynchus, Roman Egypt, 3rd century AD
papyrus_greek: Μεγάλη Ἶσις ἡ κυρία. ἀντίγραφον ἱερᾶς βίβλου τῆς εὑρεθείσης ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ ταμίοις. ὁ δὲ τρόπος ἐστὶν τὰ περὶ τὰ γράμματα κθ΄, δι’ ὧν ὁ Ἑρμῆς καὶ ἡ Ἶσις ζητοῦσα ἑαυτῆς τὸν ἀδελφὸν καὶ ἄνδρα Ὄσιριν. ἐπικαλοῦ μὲν τὸν Ἥλιον καὶ τοὺς ἐν βυθῷ θεοὺς πάντας περὶ ὧν θέλεις κληδονισθῆναι. λαβὼν φοίνικος ἄρσενος φύλλα κθ΄ ἐπίγραψον ἐν ἑκάστῳ τῶν φύλλων τὰ τῶν θεῶν ὀνόματα, καὶ ἐπευξάμενος αἶρε κατὰ δύο δύο, τὸ δὲ ὑπολειπόμενον ἔσχατον ἀναγνῶθι, καὶ εὑρήσεις σου τὴν κληδόνα, ἐν οἷς μέτεστιν, καὶ χρηματισθήσῃ τηλαυγῶς.
papyrus_english: Great is Isis, the Lady. A copy of a holy book found in the treasuries of Hermes. The method concerns the 29 letters through which Hermes, and Isis searching for Osiris, her brother and husband, [found him]. Call on the Sun and all the gods in the deep about the things on which you want an omen. Take 29 leaves of a male date palm and write on each leaf the names of the gods. Pray, then lift them two by two, and read the one left over at the last: you will find what your omen holds, and you will be answered clearly.
papyrus_note: Greek as edited by Grenfell and Hunt (1908), with their corrections of the scribe's spelling. English: our own translation. The papyrus does not list the 29 gods, and does not say what each one means.
reconstruction: The 29 gods and their answers are our own reconstruction, not ancient: gods worshipped in Roman Egypt, with Hermes, Isis and Osiris (the gods of the papyrus's story), the Sun and 'the Deep' (the gods it calls on). The answers are written for this app.
sources: B. P. Grenfell and A. S. Hunt, The Oxyrhynchus Papyri VI (1908) no. 886, pp. 200-201 (public domain).

gods.name: Hermes-Thoth
gods.egypt: Thoth, the ibis-headed scribe of the gods
gods.message: The answer is already written; you have only to read it.
gods.reading: The leaf left in your hand belongs to the keeper of the holy books, the god in whose treasuries this very oracle was found. Thoth measures, counts and records; Hermes carries the word between gods and mortals. Your question turns on something that can be learned: a fact, a letter, a conversation not yet had. Ask, read, listen. The way opens to the one who looks things up rather than guessing, and who speaks clearly rather than waiting to be understood.
gods.reflect: What do you already know that you have not yet put into words?

gods.name: Isis
gods.egypt: Great of Magic, the Lady of the papyrus
gods.message: What was scattered can be gathered again, by the one who will not stop looking.
gods.reading: Isis searched the whole of Egypt for her husband's broken body, and found it piece by piece. This is the leaf of faithful searching. Something in your life has come apart, or been lost, or seems beyond repair, and your question is whether it can be made whole. Isis answers yes, but not in one stroke. Gather what you can find today. Mourn what is missing without giving up on it. Your patience is itself a kind of magic, and she is the Lady of magic.
gods.reflect: What are you still searching for, and what have you already found?

gods.name: Osiris
gods.egypt: Lord of the West, who died and lives again
gods.message: An ending is not the end. What is buried is also planted.
gods.reading: Osiris was killed, cut apart and buried, and rose again to rule the world below; the farmers said he lived in the grain that sprouts from dark earth. Your leaf speaks of something that has ended, or is ending. Do not rush to dig it up to see whether it is alive. Seeds need their season under the soil. What comes back will not be the same as what was lost, but it will be green, and it will be yours.
gods.reflect: What in your life is lying fallow, waiting for its season?

gods.name: Horus
gods.egypt: the falcon, avenger of his father, king of the living
gods.message: Claim what is rightfully yours, and see far before you strike.
gods.reading: The falcon flies higher than any bird and sees the whole field below. Horus fought his uncle Seth for his father's throne and won it, not in a single battle but through long contest and the judgement of the gods. Your leaf says your cause is just. Stand up for it plainly, with witnesses and good order. Rise above the quarrel enough to see its true shape, and your claim will hold.
gods.reflect: Where do you need to see the whole field before you act?

gods.name: Harpocrates
gods.egypt: Horus the Child, finger to his lips
gods.gift: beginnings, silence, protection of the young
gods.message: Keep the new thing quiet and safe until it is strong enough to stand.
gods.reading: The Greeks saw the child Horus with a finger to his lips and called him the god of silence. He was hidden in the marshes as a baby while his enemies hunted him, and he grew strong in secret. What you are asking about is young: a plan, a hope, a bond, a beginning. Do not announce it yet, nor expose it to scorn or envy. Feed it quietly. Its time to be seen will come.
gods.reflect: What young thing in your life needs shelter rather than an audience?

gods.name: Sarapis
gods.egypt: lord of Alexandria, healer, giver of plenty
gods.message: Plenty is coming; make room at your table.
gods.reading: Sarapis wears a grain-measure on his head, a basket that is always full. In Alexandria the sick slept in his temple to be healed, and sailors and merchants prayed to him for a safe and profitable voyage. Your leaf is generous. Whatever you have asked about will bring more than you expected, if you meet it with an open hand. Share what comes, and it will keep coming.
gods.reflect: If abundance arrived tomorrow, who would you share it with first?

gods.name: Anubis
gods.egypt: the jackal, guide of souls and guardian of the way
gods.message: You are passing through a dark place, but you are not walking it alone.
gods.reading: The jackal knows the edges of the desert and the paths between the living and the dead; he led souls safely into the West. Your leaf says you are at a crossing: from one life to another, one role to the next, one way of seeing to a new one. It may feel like night. Anubis does not take away the dark, but he knows the road. Accept guidance from someone who has gone before you, and keep walking.
gods.reflect: Who has already walked the road you are on, and have you asked them?

gods.name: Helios-Ra, the Sun
gods.egypt: Ra, who sails the sky by day and the underworld by night
gods.gift: clarity, success, things brought into the light
gods.message: Bring it into the light. What can be seen can be done.
gods.reading: The papyrus tells you to call on the Sun before you begin, and here he answers you himself. Ra sails his boat across the sky each day and through the dark each night, and rises without fail. Your matter should be done openly: in daylight, in plain words, without secrecy. Hidden things will be shown, for good or ill; let them be. The day is on your side.
gods.reflect: What have you been keeping in the dark that would be easier in the light?

gods.name: Selene, the Moon
gods.egypt: the Moon, Khonsu the traveller and Thoth's eye of night
gods.message: Not now, but soon: watch the moon turn.
gods.reading: The moon is never the same two nights running, and yet she always returns. Ancient months began with her thin first light. Your leaf says the matter is still waxing or waning: its shape is not yet final. Do not judge by tonight's light alone. Wait for the turn, a few days or a month, and look again. What seems dark now may be full by the time you ask a second time.
gods.reflect: What changes in you with the seasons, and what stays the same?

gods.name: Amun, Zeus Ammon
gods.egypt: the Hidden One, king of the gods, with the ram's horns
gods.message: Unseen forces are working in your favour.
gods.reading: Amun's name means 'the Hidden One'. Alexander the Great crossed the desert to his oracle at Siwa and came away called the son of a god. Your leaf says there is more at work than you can see: support you have not noticed, consequences larger than the matter seems. Act with dignity, as if a king were watching, because something greater is. Your question is bigger than you think, and its answer is good.
gods.reflect: What larger story might your small question belong to?

gods.name: Ptah
gods.egypt: the craftsman who made the world by his word, Hephaestus to the Greeks
gods.message: Make it with your hands, and it will be made.
gods.reading: Ptah, god of Memphis, thought the world in his heart and spoke it with his tongue, and it was made; craftsmen called him their lord. Your leaf belongs to the workshop. The answer to your question is not luck but making: plan it, shape it, and build it piece by piece. Good tools, good measure, patient skill. What you build carefully will stand longer than you do.
gods.reflect: What could you make, rather than wait for?

gods.name: Hathor
gods.egypt: the Golden One, lady of love, music and drunkenness, Aphrodite to the Greeks
gods.message: Let joy in; it is not a distraction from your life but part of it.
gods.reading: Hathor is the Golden One, the lady of music, dancing, love and good wine. Her festivals were feasts. Your leaf says the answer lies in delight, and in the people who bring it. If your question is about love, it is a kind answer. If it is about anything else, it asks whether you have forgotten how to enjoy what you already have. Sing, dance, invite someone. Gladness opens doors that worry keeps shut.
gods.reflect: When did you last let yourself be glad without a reason?

gods.name: Bastet
gods.egypt: the cat, protector of the home and of women
gods.message: Guard your hearth, and keep your own counsel.
gods.reading: Bastet was the cat-goddess of Bubastis, where crowds came by boat to her festival. Cats guarded the granaries of Egypt from snakes and mice, and went where they pleased. Your leaf points to home: your household, your safety, your independence. Protect what is yours with a calm, watchful eye. You need not explain yourself to everyone. Be gentle with those you love, and fierce if they are threatened.
gods.reflect: What in your home most needs your protection now?

gods.name: Sobek
gods.egypt: the crocodile of the Fayum, lord of the waters
gods.gift: strength, patience, power held in reserve
gods.message: Lie still in the water. Strength waits for the right moment.
gods.reading: The crocodile lies so still in the river that he seems a log, until the moment comes. In the Fayum he was worshipped as Sobek, and sacred crocodiles wore gold in their ears. Your leaf counsels power held in reserve. Do not thrash about; do not show your hand. Watch the current. When the moment is right, you will know it, and you will need only one strong movement.
gods.reflect: Where would stillness serve you better than effort?

gods.name: Nephthys
gods.egypt: Lady of the House, sister who mourned Osiris
gods.message: Grief shared is grief carried. Sit with it a while.
gods.reading: Nephthys was Seth's wife, yet she wept for Osiris beside Isis and helped her gather him. Her name means 'Lady of the House'. Your leaf speaks of sorrow, or of loyalty in a divided family. This is not a time to decide in haste. Let the mourning have its place. Help may come from an unexpected side, from someone you thought belonged to the other camp.
gods.reflect: Who might be quietly on your side, though they seem to stand elsewhere?

gods.name: Seth-Typhon
gods.egypt: Seth, lord of the red desert and of storms, who killed Osiris
gods.message: A storm is up. Do not set out in it.
gods.reading: This is the hardest leaf. Seth killed his brother Osiris out of envy and fought Horus for years; the Greeks called him Typhon, the monster of storms. Your leaf warns of rivalry, anger or confusion around your question. Someone may not wish you well, or your own temper may be the danger. Do not go ahead now. Shelter, keep your goods close, and wait for the wind to drop. Storms pass.
gods.reflect: Is the storm outside you, or within?

gods.name: Bes
gods.egypt: the dancing dwarf-god who frightens away evil
gods.gift: protection, laughter, safe births and sleep
gods.message: Laugh at what frightens you, and it will shrink.
gods.reading: Bes was short, bearded and grotesque, sticking out his tongue and banging his drum to scare away snakes, demons and bad dreams. Every household loved him; his face was on beds and mirrors. Your leaf says you are better protected than you feel. Fear is making the matter look larger than it is. Find the funny side, keep good company, and sleep well. The danger will not survive the daylight.
gods.reflect: What fear would look smaller if you said it out loud and laughed?

gods.name: Taweret
gods.egypt: the great mother hippopotamus, guardian of birth
gods.message: Something is being born. Protect it fiercely and tenderly.
gods.reading: Taweret, 'the Great One', was a hippopotamus standing on her hind legs, swollen like a pregnant woman, with a knife in her hand to keep danger away from mothers and newborns. Your leaf speaks of birth in every sense: a child, a project, a new self. It will need strength and tenderness at once. Do not be gentle with whatever threatens it, and do not be harsh with the new thing itself.
gods.reflect: What new life are you carrying, and what does it need from you?

gods.name: Khnum
gods.egypt: the ram-headed potter who shapes each person on his wheel
gods.message: You are still on the potter's wheel; the shape is not final.
gods.reading: Khnum shaped every child on his potter's wheel and set it in its mother's womb. Clay can be wetted and reshaped until it is fired. Your leaf says the matter, or you yourself, are still being formed. Do not treat today's lumps and wobbles as your final shape. Let yourself be worked on: by teachers, by hardship, by practice. The firing comes later, and it will set what you have become.
gods.reflect: What part of you is still soft enough to change?

gods.name: Min, Pan of Egypt
gods.egypt: Min of Koptos, god of fertility and of the desert roads
gods.message: Go boldly: the road and the harvest are both open to you.
gods.reading: Min was the god of growth and of the caravan roads through the eastern desert; the Greeks called his city Panopolis, the city of Pan. Travellers left prayers to him on the rocks. Your leaf is full of life and movement. Your plans can grow and your road is open. Set out with energy, carry water, and do not dawdle at the wells. What you plant now will multiply.
gods.reflect: What would you do if you trusted your own vigour?

gods.name: Neith
gods.egypt: the archer and weaver of Sais, Athena to the Greeks
gods.message: Weave the threads carefully, then loose your arrow.
gods.reading: Neith of Sais carried crossed arrows and a weaver's shuttle. She was among the oldest of the gods and was said to have woven the world on her loom. The Greeks thought her their own Athena. Your leaf asks for both crafts: first patient weaving, bringing the threads of your plan together; then one clean, decisive shot. Do not shoot before the cloth is woven.
gods.reflect: Which threads of your plan still need tying together?

gods.name: Imhotep, Imouthes-Asclepius
gods.egypt: the wise builder and physician made a god
gods.message: Seek out the wise, and take their advice.
gods.reading: Imhotep was a real man, the architect of the first pyramid, who became a god of healing and learning; the Greeks called him Imouthes and joined him to Asclepius. Scribes poured a drop of water for him before they wrote. Your leaf is a good one for health and study. Ask an expert. Read what has been written. Take the medicine, follow the plan. Wisdom from others will heal what worry cannot.
gods.reflect: Whose advice have you been avoiding, and why?

gods.name: Agathos Daimon, the Good Spirit
gods.egypt: the serpent guardian of Alexandria and of every house
gods.gift: good luck, blessing on the household
gods.message: A good spirit watches over your house.
gods.reading: In Alexandria the Good Spirit was a serpent who guarded the city and every home; families poured him a little wine at the end of dinner. Your leaf is a blessing on your household and your plans. Things are better guarded than you know. Give thanks in small daily ways, keep your doors and promises in good order, and the good fortune will stay.
gods.reflect: What small daily thanks could you begin?

gods.name: Hapi, the Nile
gods.egypt: Hapi, the flood that feeds Egypt
gods.message: The flood comes in its season. Prepare the fields.
gods.reading: Every year the Nile rose and covered the fields with black mud, and Egypt lived on that flood. No one could hurry it; everyone prepared for it. Your leaf says your matter depends on a rising you cannot command: other people, the times, the right season. Dig your channels now, mend your dykes, have your seed ready. When the water comes, it will bring more than you could ever carry by hand.
gods.reflect: How can you prepare for a good thing you cannot hurry?

gods.name: Hecate
gods.egypt: goddess of crossroads, keys and night, beloved of the magical papyri
gods.message: You stand at a crossroads. Choose with open eyes.
gods.reading: Hecate holds torches and keys and stands where three roads meet. The magical papyri call on her more than almost any other goddess. Your leaf says you are at a fork. There is no wrong road that cannot be walked, but there is a choice you must make yourself. Light a lamp, look down each road, and take one deliberately. Do not let the night choose for you.
gods.reflect: Which road have you been pretending is not there?

gods.name: Abrasax
gods.egypt: the cock-headed, snake-legged power of the magic gems
gods.gift: protection, the turning year, hidden order
gods.message: There is an order under the confusion. Hold your shield up.
gods.reading: Abrasax appears on the magical gems of Roman Egypt with a cockerel's head, a man's body and snakes for legs, holding a shield and whip. The Greek letters of his name add up to 365, the days of the year. Your leaf promises protection and pattern. What looks like chaos has a shape you will soon see. Keep your guard up and your courage high; the year is turning your way.
gods.reflect: What pattern might you see if you stepped back from today?

gods.name: Apis
gods.egypt: the sacred bull of Memphis, herald of Ptah
gods.message: Pull steadily, and the furrow will be straight.
gods.reading: The Apis bull of Memphis was chosen by special markings and lived in a palace; people came to watch which way he turned, and took it as an oracle. Your leaf is about strength used steadily: the ox at the plough, not the bull in the ring. Keep going at a pace you can hold. Your work will bear fruit, and others will notice your strength more than your speed.
gods.reflect: What would change if you worked at a pace you could keep for years?

gods.name: Agathe Tyche, Good Fortune
gods.egypt: the city's Fortune, partner of the Good Spirit
gods.message: Fortune has turned towards you. Take the chance while it is offered.
gods.reading: Good Fortune held a horn of plenty and a ship's rudder: she gives, and she steers. In Alexandria she stood beside the Good Spirit as the luck of the city. Your leaf says an opportunity is near, perhaps already in front of you. Luck is real, but it favours the prepared. Notice the opening, step through it, and steer well once you are on your way.
gods.reflect: What opportunity is in front of you that you have not yet taken?

gods.name: The Deep
gods.egypt: the primeval waters from which all things rose, where the papyrus's gods dwell
gods.message: The answer lies deeper than the question. Go down before you go on.
gods.reading: The papyrus calls on 'all the gods in the deep'. The Egyptians said that before anything existed there was only the dark, endless water, and that the first hill rose from it at the beginning of the world. Your leaf takes you below the surface of your question. What do you really want? What are you really afraid of? Rest, dream, listen. When you understand what lies underneath, the answer will rise on its own, like land from the flood.
gods.reflect: What is the question beneath your question?
